Interpreting the July 26, 2017 FOMC statement through the lens of the literature suggests a modestly dovish tilt despite continued labor-market strength. In the Clarida–Galí–Gertler framework, the Committee’s emphasis on “gradual” adjustments and explicit interest-rate smoothing is consistent with a policy rule that reacts cautiously when inflation is below target and expectations appear anchored. The statement notes that “overall inflation and the measure excluding food and energy prices have declined and are running below 2 percent,” and that “market-based measures of inflation compensation remain low,” which aligns with inflation-forecast targeting principles (Svensson and Woodford) that warrant patience until projected inflation converges sustainably to target. Sticky-price New Keynesian transmission (Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans) also implies muted near-term inflation pressure when slack and expectations anchor inflation, supporting gradualism. While the announcement of balance-sheet normalization “relatively soon” nods to eventual policy normalization (Goodfriend on operating frameworks), the explicit monitoring of inflation “closely” and the reiteration of a symmetric 2 percent goal skew the tone slightly dovish relative to neutral—incrementally supportive for risk assets.

"Job gains have been solid, on average, since the beginning of the year, and the unemployment rate has declined."
